question: In Computers, files when deleted are moved to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Recycle Bin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is a special folder used to store deleted files temporarily.
 
• When files are deleted from the computer, they are moved to the Recycle Bin instead of being permanently erased, allowing users to recover them if needed.
 
• The Recycle Bin is typically represented by an icon on the desktop, resembling a trash can.
 
• Files in the Recycle Bin can be restored to their original location or permanently deleted to free up space on the hard drive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **My Documents**

 
 
• My Documents is a default folder in Windows operating systems used to store personal documents and files.
 
• It is typically located in the user's profile directory and serves as a centralized location for documents.
 
• Files stored here are not deleted when moved to the Recycle Bin.
 
 
 
• **Inbox**
 
 
• The Inbox is a folder in email applications where incoming messages are stored.
 
• It is the primary location for new emails received by the user.
 
• Deleting emails from the inbox usually moves them to a Trash or Deleted Items folder within the email application.
 
 
 
• **Outbox**
 
 
• The Outbox is a folder in email applications where outgoing messages are temporarily stored before being sent.
 
• Emails in the Outbox are waiting to be processed and sent to their recipients.
 
• Once the emails are successfully sent, they are typically moved to the Sent Items folder.
